texts.preamble: Srinivasan. S vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Kabc0B0016272022 Before The Mact & Xv Addl., Judge, Court Of Small Causes, (Scch-19) Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru. Dated this the 27th day of February 2025 Present: Sri. Mohan Sadashiv Pol, B.A.Ll.B. (Spl.) Xv Addl. Small Causes Judge & Xxiii Acmm, Bengaluru. MVC.No.6374/2022 1) Sri. Srinivasan S. S/o. Sanmugam, Age 40 years, R/at No.B/5-06, Ksdb Quarters, Opp Loyal Retail Mart, Kudlu, Bangalore-560 068. ....Petitioner (By Sri. T.M. Adv.,) -V/s- 1) The Managing Director, Motor Claims Hub, Ksrtc Shanthinagar, Bengaluru - 560027 . (Owner of KSRTC Bus bearing KA-57/F-3773) 2) Sri. Vasanth Kumar M. S/o. Munivenkatappa, SCCH - 19 2 MVC.6374/2022 Attivata Village, Dasarahalli, Joddidasarahalli, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District-562 114. (Owner of Lorry bearing No.KA-16/D-9498) 3) Sri. Srinivasa S/o. Chikka Venkatagiriyappa, Valagerepura Village, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District-562 114.
texts.facts: The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 claiming compensation from the respondents due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. 2. Brief facts of petitioner's case is that on 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 p.m, the petitioner was traveling in KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, on Kolar-Bangalore NH Road, when the bus reached opposite to NH-75 Hotel, near Mylapura Gate Hosakote, Bangalore Rural District, the driver of said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed to one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498, which was parked on the road by its driver without any precaution, as a result of forced impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries. 3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and wherein the duty doctors examined him clinically and radiologically, which revealed that he sustained Haemotama over forehead and all the injuries treated with conservatively and he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food, transportation, conveyance and other charges. Due to the said accidental injuries, the petitioner completely bed ridden, cannot run, jump, cannot lift or carry any weight, unable to sleep properly, she cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering, since the injuries caused permanent in nature. Srinivasan.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171203603/ 2 4. It is contended that, this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 and also due to negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D- 9498. Hence, the Hosakote Police have registered a case against drivers of said vehicles in crime No.353/2022. 5. It is contended that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale, healthy, aged about 40 years and he was having own Printing Press and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries he is not able to do her job and hence he lost his earning and suffering from mental shock and agony and also facing great financial difficulties. 6. The respondent No.1 being owner of the KSRTC Bus, Respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the Lorry, respondent No.3 being insurer of the Lorry and respondent No.4 is the insurance company of the Lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, this petition was filed against the respondents for claiming compensation. 7. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent No.1 to 4 appeared through their respective counsel and the respondent No.2 and 3 have filed joint written statement and the respondent No.1 and 4 have filed their written statements separately. 8. Brief contents of the written statement of respondent No.1 is that while admitting the ownership of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this respondent contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 as he was parked the Lorry in the middle of the road without any precautionary measurement and signals. Hence, respondent No.2 to 4 are liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner. However, on humanitarian ground this respondent paid the entire hospital bill amounting to Rs.26,206/- and same may be liable to be deducted and in case of holding contributory negligence on the part of the Lorry either fully or partially. The insurer and owner of the lorry shall be directed to refund the medical expenses paid by this respondent to the petitioner to the extent of their liability. Further, it has denied the date, place, mode of accident and nature of injuries, age, income, occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by her and disability caused to her and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition. 9. Brief contents of the written statement of respondent No.2 and 3 are that the petition filed by the petition is not maintainable neither under facts of the case nor under the question of law and it is to be dismissed in limine. It is further contended that these respondents are the owner and driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 who parked left side of the road and taken the required all safety and precautionary methods with due diligence, because of the negligent and rash driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this accident was happened and the Bus suddenly came to the footpath and hit the lorry, the driver of the said bus drove the same beyond speed limits in a negligent manner without applying breaks. The petitioner has filed this false case against the respondent No.2 and 3 with malafide intention in view of getting higher compensation and as the respondent No.1 who is the manager of the KSRTC Bus is vicariously liable for the conduct of the bus driver, so, he being solely responsible for the compensation. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition against these respondents. In order to substantiate the case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 08 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8. 15 . Issue No.1:- The petitioner filed this petition under against respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. 20. Issue No.2:- The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.5,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident. The petitioner produced wound certificate issued by Silicon City Hospital, Hosakote, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.
texts.arguments: The respondent No.4 has contended in his written statement that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition. While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/ D-9498, this respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further contended that, driver of the said vehicle did not possess valid D.L. FC and permit as on the date of the accident and hence, terms and conditions of the insurance policy were violated. It is contended that, this accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, as the driver of Lorry was parked his vehicle with all precautionary measures with signals to other vehicles. Further these respondents denied the date, place and mode of accident, age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to her and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with costs. 11. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required. 19. The petitioner has sustained simple injury and not treated as an inpatient. Hence, the petitioner is not entitled any compensation under the head loss of income during laid up period and also loss of amenities in life.
